unit.title: Public Goods, Taxes, and Community Choices

lesson.title: Review Day: Public Goods, Taxes, and Community Choices
lesson.subject: social-studies

contentBlocks.text: This week you learned how communities pay for and choose shared things. Let's review it all!

Quick review: a public good is paid for by the whole community, unlike a private good (Day 1). Taxes are the shared money that pays for public goods (Day 2). Firefighters, teachers, and librarians are real tax-funded jobs (Day 3). Communities have to choose between public goods since money is limited (Day 4). Answer: what makes a good 'public' instead of 'private'? Name one tax-funded job and explain who it helps.
Wonderful work this week — you learned how a whole community works together to pay for and choose shared things! Next week we'll explore something new.

objectives: Review public vs. private goods, taxes, tax-funded jobs, and community decision-making
Explain what makes a good public and name one tax-funded job and who it helps
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child explain the public-vs-private distinction in their own words.
3. Have the child name one tax-funded job and who it helps.
4. Complete the review worksheet.
5. Celebrate finishing a full week of community-economics learning!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the public-vs-private distinction, the foundation the rest of the week builds on
Ready for more: ask the child to connect this week's ideas back to last week's goods/services/trade vocabulary in one sentence
This is a good checkpoint to note whether the child needs more practice on the public-goods concept specifically before the next Social Studies unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a recall and review activity — check that the child can explain public goods are paid for by the whole community (not one person) and correctly name one tax-funded job with who it helps.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's C3 Framework Economics and Civics dimensions before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
